source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Broad-headed small tree with arching branches
morphology_documented.wood_bark_roots: Yellow to orange wood; roots prominently orange; milky sap
morphology_documented.leaves: Alternate entire elliptic to ovate-lanceolate leaves, pointed, glabrous above and sparsely pubescent beneath
morphology_documented.flowers: Dioecious; staminate flowers in short-peduncled oblong-ovoid dense clusters; pistillate on separate trees in globose heads with conspicuous elongated styles
morphology_documented.fruit: Wrinkled green/yellow-green multiple fruit up to 12 cm or more across; individual achenes embedded in fleshy calyces
morphology_documented.habitat: Stream bottoms, lower slopes, disturbed limestone uplands

source_scope_note: Genus and key details explicitly noted; where historical flora lacks a species treatment, morphology is limited to independently named secondary sources.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Flora indicates pre-settlement native area much smaller than modern occurrences; historical planting for hedges has greatly broadened range
Even though North American native in a restricted region, Hays natural nativity must be BONAP county checked; no Texas-wide assumption
preservation: Additive, original taxon records, photos, attribution and site unchanged
